{{Quote|During the parade, I looked out over the cheering crowds of Gungans and Naboo. My beautiful emerald world is free. We have made peace. The camps have been demolished. The people have returned to their homes.|Queen Amidala|<ref name="E1J:QA">''[[Star Wars Journal: Queen Amidala]]''</ref>}}
The '''Freedom Day''' celebrations were organized on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] following the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|victory]] against the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] invasion forces in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. Back by popular demand, a triumph parade was scheduled to be the high point of those celebrations two days after the decisive battle. [[King/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]], the [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Monarch of Naboo]], first intended to call off the parade, arguing that the loss of the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] during the conflict demanded mourning rather than revelry. However, the Queen experienced a change of heart after a discussion with [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], Master Jinn's former [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]]. The triumphal parade moved through the streets of Theed, reaching its endpoint at the steps of the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Royal Palace]]. In addition to the parade, a number of artistic venues of Theed opened their doors to the general public, offering [[Gungan sling painting]] perfomances, puppet shows and concerts. For their part, the Gungans organized a funfair in [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], their underwater capital.

==History==
{{Quote|The Queen be keeping her promise. Looks like wesa winning after all.|Bombad General Binks reacting to the battle droids' deactivation|<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' (junior novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:TF_Battleship.png|thumb|left|250px|A Trade Federation ship forms a blockade around Naboo.]]
In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] conducted an illegal [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|blockade]] of [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], a member world of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] leaders of the Trade Federation sent their [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|army]] to the surface of the planet. With the help of two [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], the two native peoples of the planet, the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] and the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]], united against the invasion.<ref name="TPM" /> In effect, two battles were [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|fought simultaneously]]. While the Gungans confronted the bulk of the droid infantry on the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]], the [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] of the Nabooian [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Squadron]] sought to destroy the [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|''Vuutun Palaa'']], the Federation's [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|control Ship]], which commanded the droid army down on Naboo.<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> The victory was sealed when the young [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] unexpectedly landed a [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighter]] into the heart of the Control Ship, firing [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] into its reactor. The resulting explosion destroyed the ship, hereby rendering the mechanized army useless.<ref name="TPM" />

Together, the Naboo resistance had driven the Trade Federation out of their homeland. The [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen of Naboo]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], who had shown heroic conduct throughout the crisis, had formed an newfound alliance with the Gungans represented by [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]]. The victory on Naboo was a major one, but at an enormous [[Death/Legends|cost]] in lives. No less than 543 Gungans had lost their lives on the battlefield,<ref name="GB Databank">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' Databank: [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] civilization entry</ref> and Master Qui-Gon Jinn had been killed by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] known as [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] while dueling in Theed's [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] [[Plasma Refinery Complex|Refinery Complex]].<ref name="TPM" />

===Preparations===
{{Quote|Qui-Gon's funeral was attended by many Jedi Masters and as many people of Naboo that could crowd into the plaza. Afterward, I went to see Obi-Wan. The people have called for a victory parade, and one has been scheduled. I wanted to call it off. A joyous parade felt wrong, with Qui-Gon gone.|Queen Amidala|<ref name="E1J:QA" />}}
[[File:Mourning_Qui-Gon.png|thumb|250px|The Queen nearly cancelled the celebrations out of regard for the late Qui-Gon Jinn.]]
In the aftermath of the decisive battle that was fought on the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]], the [[Prison/Legends|prison]] camps built by the Trade Federation were quickly dismantled, and the people of Naboo expected an official time of revelry. Their call was heard, and a triumph parade was planned. However, before anything else could be done, the Queen had to organize a decent [[Funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|funeral]] for the late Jedi Master Jinn. On the day after the battle, Jinn's body was [[Cremation/Legends|cremated]] on a solemn pyre in the [[Theed Funeral Temple/Legends|Funeral Temple]] of Theed, a quiet building with an open ceiling. When Queen Amidala attended the funeral ceremony, she was deeply affected; she thought a day of parade would come too soon and would feel inappropriate when a great hero such as Qui-Gon Jinn had died. The Queen then asked the young Obi-Wan Kenobi for advice, confessing she wished to cancel the parade out of respect for the deceased. However, Kenobi comforted the sorrowful queen and told her Master Jinn would have wanted the parade to happen, calling for life to regain its rights over death and sadness. Amidala reconsidered her decision, now committed to let a triumph ceremony take place the day after the funeral.<ref name="E1J:QA" />

===The parade===
{{Quote|The next day cheers of joy ring in the streets as we celebrate our triumph. Our lives on Naboo will never be the same. We Gungans have joined with the Queen and her people in the name of justice. Our people are now friends, joined together in the name of peace.|Boss Nass|<ref name="Gungan Trouble!">''[[Gungan Trouble!]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Theed_youth_freedom.png|thumb|left|250px|The children of Naboo celebrate the victory over the Trade Federation.]]
The Grand Army and the [[Great Municipal Band/Legends|Great Municipal Band]] led by [[Augara Jowil/Legends|Augara Jowil]] gathered to form a massive Gungan procession through the streets of Theed. For their part, citizens of the Naboo [[Capital/Legends|capital]] gathered on the sides of the [[Palace Plaza/Legends|Palace Plaza]] with arms full of colored ribbons and cut [[Plant/Legends|flowers]]. On the city's grandest square, columns of Gungan warriors and musicians marched through Theed to the sounds of cheering and singing.<ref name="TMPN" /> While marching toward the steps of the Palace, the Great Municipal Band played the first movement of the "[[Symponik Nabooalla]]"&mdash;literally "the epic for all of Naboo"&mdash;a musical piece composed by Jowil for this event.<ref name="DBAug">{{DB|character|augie|Jowil, Augara "Augie"}}</ref> On the sides, children threw flowers, and the streets were full of laughters. The marching Gungans were led by Boss Nass, who rode a ceremonial [[Falumpaset/Legends|falumpaset]]. [[Bombad General/Legends|Bombad General]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] and [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Roos Tarpals/Legends|Roos Tarpals]] acted as their Boss' guard of honor, mounting their own kaadu. The old Tarpals had been given a senior position in the parade, which filled him with deserved pride, following his heroic participation in the Battle of the Grassy Plains.<ref name="FF">{{FactFile|108|VIC 1-4|Victory on Naboo}}</ref>

Queen Amidala stood at the top of the stone steps, with the newly elected [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], the twelve members of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]],<ref name="TMPN" /> Obi-Wan Kenobi and the young Anakin Skywalker. The Queen's own guards, the pilots of the Naboo Space Fighter Corps and a few dignitaries also watched the parade approach from the Palace's steps, in the shadow of the statues of ancient [[Naboo philosophers]].<ref name="TPM" /> Several members of the Chancellor's [[Senate Guard/Legends|Blue Guard]] also stood at attention.<ref name="Snap" />

The Queen presented her Gungan counterpart with the [[Globe of Peace/Legends|Globe of Peace]], a hallowed Naboo artifact from the days of yore. Nass, who was extremely skilled at public displays, knew how to send an assembly wild with excitement. He turned to the crowds and lifted the Globe in a dramatic gesture, shouting the keyword of the day: "Peace!"<ref name="TPM" /> The assembled Gungans, thrilled with joy, immediately broke columns and started dancing about on the plaza.<ref name="TMPN" /> Whereas some people had initially doubted Amidala's leadership abilities due to her young age, the Queen knew that such distrust had melted away when she gazed at the citizens of Naboo, Humans and Gungans together.<ref name="Sn!">''[[Save Naboo!]]''</ref> The joint victory ceremony between the Gungans and the Naboo was the largest and grandest ever recorded on that planet.<ref name="NFF5">{{FactFile2013|5|NAB 3-6|Naboo: Theed}}</ref>

===The public attractions===
[[File:Amidala_on_the_Coliseum_plaza.png|thumb|200px|In Theed, the Coliseum Plaza hosted a series of attractions.]]
{{Quote|At the Theed Coliseum, you can try Gungan Sling Painting. There, you will help Gungans paint dancing droids!|Queen Amidala|<ref name="ELAC">''[[Star Wars: Early Learning Activity Center]]''</ref>}}
While the parade itself was meant to represent the formal side of the celebration, popular merry-making was also organized in the streets of Theed and [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], the underwater capital city of the Gungans. In Theed, the entertainment venues of the [[Theed Coliseum Plaza|Coliseum Plaza]] threw open their doors to visitors. In the city's funnel-shaped [[Theed Coliseum|Coliseum]], a performance of [[Gungan sling painting|sling painting]] by the [[Gungan Sling Brigade]] was held, to the delight of the crowd. The [[Theed Music Hall]] and the [[Naboo Puppet Theater]] also offered free spectacles within their fields. Meanwhile, at the Gungan funfair, visitors were invited to dance the [[deesco]] with Jar Jar Binks at the "Deesco Bubble," try to [[Gungan dunk tank|dunk]] Boss Nass in a clear water tank at the "Dunk Boss Nass Bubble", or search hidden [[Clam/Legends|clams]] in a water-filled cave with the Jedi Knight Obi-Wan Kenobi&mdash;who had accepted to play the game with enthusiasm. Although he was now a [[Padawan/Legends|Jedi apprentice]] under the tutelage of Kenobi, the young Anakin Skywalker also enjoyed his share of amusement in the lively streets of Theed.<ref name="ELAC" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:BibbleGlobeOfPeace-EpisodeIInsidersGuide.png|thumb|right|150px|[[Oliver Ford Davies]] (playing Governor Sio Bibble) holding a glass ball&mdash;which was transformed into the Globe of Peace in postproduction]]
The triumphal parade featured at the end of the [[1999]] movie [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] was already present in the first version of the script. In this version, the [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] of the Trade Federation [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] and his aide [[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]] were brought before the Queen, in chains and under the surveillance of Gungan guards. Additionally, Amidala would not offer the Globe of Peace to Rugor Nass, although it was still obvious that the Naboo and Gungans had become allies.<ref name="E1:IG">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref> While the scene seems like a happy ending, it marks Palpatine's first step toward [[Galactic Empire/Legends|galactic domination]]. Accordingly, the cheerful music played by the band was actually a reworking of "[[The Emperor's Theme]]," a dark vocal piece first heard in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="SWI109">{{InsiderCite|109|Menace Revisited}}</ref> The video game [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]] also contains the celebration scene at the end of its last mission, but it utilizes the track "Hail to the, Winner, Anakin Skywalker" instead of "Augie's Great Municipal Band."<ref name="TPMVG">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref>

Most of the scene was realized in CGI by an [[Industrial Light & Magic]] visual effects team under the direction of [[Scott Squires]]. The team added many CGI characters and creatures, increased the quantity of colorful confetti and modified the lighting so the parade appeared to take place at sunset.<ref name="E1:IG" />

In the [[2010]] book of artworks ''[[Star Wars Art: Visions]]'', the [[Wikipedia:United States of America|American]] classic painter [[Allan R. Banks]] depicted the children of Theed rejoicing during the victory parade. Banks' artwork title was ''Celebration of Naboo Youth on Freedom Day'', which suggests the official name of the victory celebration was "Freedom Day."<ref name="SWA:V">''[[Star Wars Art: Visions]]''</ref>
